start_here: Say to your AI: "Score which of my folders ./current and ./candidate sounds most like the real speaker in ref.wav."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it takes a reference recording and folders of line recordings and prints scores.
instructions: 1. Put each voice model's lines in one folder with the same file names (l01.wav, l02.wav).

2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:score-how-alike-lines-sound-to-a-reference-voice"}, installs torch and pyannote.audio if missing and runs the command in given; the first run needs HF_HUB_OFFLINE=0 once so the speaker model downloads.
3. Read the last line: each folder's lines and mean. Higher is more alike (same-speaker pairs score well above 0.5).
4. Tell the person which folder is closest and that this is likeness only: listen too.

worked_examples.title: Two folders scored against the speaker's reference
worked_examples.ask: Which folder sounds most like the real speaker?
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/compare-voice-and-music-models/do-work/speaker_similarity.py; its score step is tested in tools/compare-voice-and-music-models/test/test_compare_models.py (cosine of 1.0 and 0.6 for two lines gives mean 0.8). Run: python3 -I tools/compare-voice-and-music-models/do-work/speaker_similarity.py ref.wav ./current ./candidate with l01.wav and l02.wav in each folder.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"reference":"ref.wav","model":"pyannote/wespeaker-voxceleb-resnet34-LM","folders":[{"dir":"./current","lines":{"l01.wav":<cosine>,"l02.wav":<cosine>},"mean":<mean of the two>},{"dir":"./candidate","lines":{...},"mean":...}]}}: each line is the cosine of its voice embedding with the reference, rounded to 3 places, and the mean is per folder (a folder with no matching file has mean null). A missing folder answers {"error":"./nowhere is not a folder: pass one folder of line recordings per voice model"}.
